text:
Marta R.: quick question — for the inference fleet, are we leaning toward agent-side OTLP (sidecar/collector) vs services exporting directly to OTLP? thinking about buffering, shutdown flush, and retention costs
Sanjay: agent-side seems nicer for languages that don't have great shutdown semantics (rust/python fast-exit). less double-config for routes too
Olivia P: +1 for agent, but we lose some per-request context unless we propagate extra attrs. we should avoid adding PII to spans though
Ryan: if we go agent, we should make the agent understand model_id/route_id header so it can attach attributes. otherwise dashboards will be noisy
Marta R.: agree on model_id. also worried about batching processor defaults — we see long schedule_delay in some services and tokens pile up. need sane defaults for inference (low latency flush)
Sanjay: propose defaults: max_queue_size=2000, schedule_delay_millis=50, max_export_batch_size=512 for GPU-backed services. larger for batch workers
Olivia P: also remember memory pressure on tiny sidecars in Dedicated pods. maybe have agent support a "lite" profile that uses smaller queues and backpressure to the caller
Aisha: how do we handle shutdown? services often get SIGTERM and have ~10s. the Python SDK's shutdown sometimes hangs waiting on background thread. we should ensure quick flush via explicit force_flush in our signal handler
Ryan: we already added a pattern in router: on SIGTERM call tracer.force_flush(timeout=3000) then sleep 50ms, then exit. but not all languages have consistent API. that's why agent path is nice — agent keeps exporting after process dies for a bit
DeployBot: deploy: infra/telemetry updated collector image to 0.21.2 — rollout started :rocket:
Sanjay: downside of agent is retention/cost: if every service sends everything, ingestion blows up. need sampling and attribute filtering at the source or collector pipeline to drop large attributes like full prompts
Marta R.: decision points:
- require model_id and request_id attrs at service level (env var to opt-out)
- default sampling: 1% for embeddings-heavy routes, 100% for failures and high-latency traces
- redact prompt_text & input_tokens at SDK layer unless ENABLE_PROMPT_CAPTURE=true
- prefer agent for runtime languages with bad shutdown; allow direct OTLP from go/rust with proper shutdown hooks
Olivia P: for console dashboards we map trace.request_id -> span.resource.service.instance to aggregate per-route latency. need to standardize attribute names: `redwood.model_id`, `redwood.route`, `redwood.request_id`
Sanjay: also add `redwood.kv_cache_hit` boolean and `redwood.token_delta` int for cost analysis (careful with cardinality)
Aisha: can we put a small code snippet in devex docs for Python + Go showing recommended SDK config and shutdown handler? I can draft if we agree on defaults
Marta R.: please do. one more: exporter topology — prefer local agent + OTLP/gRPC to collector. fallback to direct OTLP endpoint in env (REDWOOD_OTLP_ENDPOINT) for private/onprem deployments
Ryan: PR incoming to add env flags and a small lifecycle helper in our internal SDK wrappers: `RedwoodTracer.init(collector_addr=None, profile='inference')`
Olivia P: sounds good. I'll add the attribute naming to telemetry schema doc and wire up the console mapping
Sanjay: small note — test plan: simulate pod preemption to validate force_flush works and agent continues export for 10s after process exit
Marta R.: thanks everyone. Aisha please share the sample snippets here when done and we'll lock defaults in a follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
